newsitem.title: USA: Dow lower at midday on Kodak, tobacco losses.
newsitem.headline: Dow lower at midday on Kodak, tobacco losses.

text.p: A big drop in Eastman Kodak Co. shares and steady losses in tobacco stocks weighed down blue-chip stocks Friday in otherwise listless trading.

The Dow Jones industrial average was down 17.75 points at 6,802.53 at 1 p.m. EST. In the broader market, advancing issues held a narrow 6-5 lead over declines on active volume of 343 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Investors were seen biding their time before a Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday that could bring higher interest rates, traders said.

"The market is searching for a trading range between here and 7,000 (on the Dow). It may be ... lower until we get a clear-cut idea what the Fed is going to do," said Steven van Brunt, equity trader at Nikko Securities.
Kodak shares were off 10-1/8 at 78-1/8 on heavy volume after the photographic giant disclosed flat sales for January and February compared with a year earlier.
"Kodak is the main drag on the Dow. The Nasdaq Composite, the Dow transports are on the plus side and the bond market was up a little bit," said Doug Myers, equity trader at Interstate Johnson Lane.

The Nasdaq Composite was up 2.16 points at 1,262.42, but the 30-year Treasury bond had turned slightly negative by midday, off an eighth of a point. Its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, was at 6.97 percent.
Philip Morris Cos. continued to fall in the wake of Thursday's settlement of class-action litigation by its competitor, Brooke Group Ltd.'s Liggett Group.
Most other shares traded quietly, with many market players banking on a slow erosion in prices to set the stage for bargain-hunting in coming sessions.
"Traders are not taking big positions because there's a feeling out there that if you just wait, you'll get your stock," said Myers.
Traders played down the impact of Friday's triple witching options expirations, noting that much of the anticipatory position-shifting occurred earlier in the week.
"A lot of our stocks are mixed. You get this type of reaction on Friday because a lot of the volatility occurs on the Thursdays of triple-witching weeks," said Myers.

Technology shares generally held steady after a brief rally on Thursday. The technology sector had been under heavy pressure over the preceding two weeks, and traders hesitated to take aggressive positions in either direction.
Adding to the Dow's decline was a 3-5/8 drop to 133 in the stock of International Business Machines Corp.

Tech stocks are considered especially sensitive to interest rate hikes and have sold off substantially as expectations have risen that the Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee will boost rates when it meets on Tuesday.
Despite ample discussion, traders said they had reached no conclusion on the likely market reaction to a Fed rate hike.

"There are a million opinions, including that the market has already priced in a 25-basis-point increase in the Fed funds rate (to 5.5 percent)," said van Brunt. "The market appears to be saying a rate hike is going to happen, but how much, we don't know."
